speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You've described a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any red streaks spreading from the wound, fever, or a recent insect bite? Also, do you have any history of diabetes or circulation problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Sarcoidosis (likely secondary to ant bite), given the history of anterior uveitis and Crohn's disease, though necrotizing fasciitis must be ruled out immediately due to the ulcerative nature in a diabetic patient. I will request images of the lesion to assess the depth and extent of tissue involvement.
